priorities.issue: Five rows by two columns leave each data panel vertically shallow at reading size; policy names are legible but details and confidence bands are small.
priorities.proposed_change: Increase overall figure height approximately15to20percent while retaining all ten panels, shared scales, policy labels, shock shading and original intervals; allow following prose to flow naturally.

priorities.issue: Five shock-response panels are vertically compressed; bands are small and page has lower available whitespace.
priorities.proposed_change: Increase overall figure height approximately15to20percent, retain common scales, true zero and all original data/bands.

priorities.issue: Two-line population/horizon labels are close between adjacent groups, especially10000/100000 at reading size.
priorities.proposed_change: Shorten only display population labels to1k/10k/100k with full values and Tdays retained in caption/table; preserve four actual workloads and cold/warm markers; modest panelheight increase if pageflow permits.

priorities.issue: Six parameter-recovery rows have tight vertical spacing; compact table and small footnote precede long prose.
priorities.proposed_change: Increase row spacing locally; preserve every original numeric value and exact heldout definition.

priorities.issue: Nine-column benchmark table is compact with tight rows and unused lower page area.
priorities.proposed_change: Increase row spacing locally; use header linebreaks only if needed, preserving timing/units/executed horizon and every numeric value.

record.whitespace_interpretation: Title/abstract, references end and final appendix whitespace are intentional. Lower whitespace on several float-led result pages is partly a float-pagination consequence; filling every gap would harm hierarchy. Prioritise increased plot object height and table row pitch where it improves reading.
